text:
jess: Heads-up — spotted a regression in canary for /generate: packets show a sustained p95 bump but our canary alert didn't fire. Screenshot in thread.
mike: link?
jess: https://dash.redwood.dev/d/rollouts/canary-overview?orgId=1&view=generate - look at 02:10->02:20 window, p95 jumps ~30% for canary only.
anya: Ugh. I think the dashboard aggregates across regions, so short regional regressions get washed out. We should show canary vs baseline by percentile (p50/p95/p99) and region/model-variant.
sam: Also add error-rate delta. Average latency alone is misleading for tail regressions. Can we compute relative increase instead of absolute?
jess: Proposal: new panels for p50/p95/p99, error rate %, and request success rate. Add drilldowns: route, model.variant, region, and top-10 request IDs. For alerting: require both latency and error signal to reduce noise.
mike: Sounds good. Draft alert suggestion (PromQL-like) for the ops repo:
```
alert: CanaryLatencyRegression
expr: |
  (p95_latency_seconds{env="canary"} / p95_latency_seconds{env="baseline"}) > 1.25
  and
  (increase(errors_total{env="canary"}[5m]) - increase(errors_total{env="baseline"}[5m])) > 0.005
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Canary p95 > 25% baseline and error delta > 0.5%"
```
anya: Love the dual-guard. Maybe make the error delta relative to baseline traffic to avoid tiny-traffic flukes: (errors_canary / requests_canary) - (errors_baseline / requests_baseline) > 0.005.
sam: UX request: when someone clicks the canary panel, expand into a small sample view with recent traces (link to Jaeger) and top prompts. Engineers want to quickly decide rollback vs keep.
jess: Also add a lightweight 'suggested-action' on the dashboard: button to abort canary rollout (calls internal API) and adds a rollback tag. Should require two approvals.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout 0.23.4 -> 0.24.0 started by @mike :rocket:
mike: I can PR the dashboard panels + alert rule this afternoon. jess, can you add the drilldown wireframe? I'll co-review after standup.
anya: I'll run the query across last 30 days to get baseline ratios and propose tuned thresholds.
jess: Thanks. If everyone agrees, we'll ship as opt-in for the next canary batch and monitor false positives for 2 weeks. :thumbsup:
